The Argand diagram above shows the roots of the cubic polynomial $f(x).$ Find $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $5.$

$f(x)=$
{{field-1}}${x}^{3}\,-$
{{field-2}}${x}^{2}\,+$
{{field-3}}$x\,-$
{{field-4}}
worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2,3}=3\pm 2\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=5.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =5(x-1)(x-(3+2\text{i}))(x-(3-2\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5(x-1)(x-(3+2\text{i}))(x-(3-2\text{i})) & = \\ 5(x-1)({x}^{2}-x(3-2\text{i})-x(3+2\text{i})+(3+2\text{i})(3-2\text{i})) & = \\ 5(x-1)({x}^{2}-6x+13) & = \\ 5({x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+13x-{x}^{2}+6x-13) & = \\ 5{x}^{3}-35{x}^{2}+95x-65.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=5{x}^{3}-35{x}^{2}+95x-65.$
